question: Does replacing R127's one-expert persistent MoE scheduler and per-call atomic allocation with an exact dense output-tile grid bring the validated fixed-M32 BLOCK_FP8 arithmetic inside both latency gates?

only_semantic_change_from_r127.description: Launch exactly ceil(M/32)*ceil(N/64) workgroups and derive each independent (m_tile,n_tile) coordinate from group_linear_id. Remove the rows tensor from device use, the allocated atomic scratch, the global atomic work queue, and the persistent all-SM launch. Keep xe_gemm_4bits<BLOCK_FP8,128>, its M32 policy, scale indexing, DPAS reduction, layouts, and output store unchanged.

candidate_artifacts.note: The extension is byte-identical because the changed AOT kernel resides in its linked grouped-GEMM device library.
candidate_artifacts.abi_and_registration_check: Passed in the exact R62 container with no GPU devices; candidate operators registered under Torch 2.13.0+xpu. No XPU tensor was allocated.

gates.identity_and_numerical: Unchanged from R127: one row-0 class, every M512 prefix exact, M200 permutation/repeat exact, M168 random appended-row content exact, finite, and max absolute error versus oneDNN <=0.06 on both shapes.
gates.latency_for_expansion: Unchanged from R127: for both shapes, geometric-mean candidate/control across timed M <=1.15 and no individual M >1.50x.
gates.health: No new Xe fault, reset, timeout, hang, coredump, or device loss.
gates.on_pass: Expand this exact direct-grid kernel to all six production W8A16 shapes and model full-step overhead before any server build.
gates.on_failure: Preserve and classify the result. Do not launch a server. Further kernel work requires a measured mechanism beyond scheduler/allocation removal.
